title: Second Sight
logline: At a visiting eye camp, dressings come off one by one, and each patient's first sight in months depends on a surgeon, a donor, a driver, a nurse and a lens ground somewhere else entirely.
human_question: How many other people does it take before one person can simply see again?

premise.story: A mobile cataract-surgery camp from the first morning's queue to the moment bandages come off, following patients, the visiting surgical team and the local volunteers who make the camp possible.
premise.place: A rural hospital or temple hall hosting a visiting eye-surgery team.
premise.experience: The camera stays close to hands and eyes: the wait in dim light, the operation itself glimpsed only briefly, and the exact instant someone reads a chart, names a colour or sees a face again.

concept_links.why: Both sources use the eye as their example of a governing faculty: clarity of sight can be no clearer than the eye allows; the camp shows one faculty restored and what depends on it changing.
Pre-nascence: something already there, the eye and its base, supports what arises after it; restoring that base organ is a literal, filmable version of the relation.

what_camera_could_observe: Queues on the first morning, led in by relatives
The ward after surgery, bandages still on
Bandages coming off; a patient identifying colours or a relative's face
First attempts to thread a needle, read a bus number or walk unaided
The visiting team packing up to move on to the next town
what_must_be_real: Patients' real consent and real outcomes, including cases where sight is not fully restored; the team's real schedule and constraints.

possible_arc.opening: A queue in half-light, people led by relatives who see for them.
possible_arc.turn: The operations happen, mostly out of frame; the ward waits.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever patients actually see and say when the bandage comes off.

position_hint: closing candidate: restoring a faculty that had failed is a filmable image of a condition undone, echoing the group's hand-off that what arises by conditions can also cease by conditions

requirements: A visiting eye-surgery camp with willing patients, surgeons and organisers
Clear, ongoing informed consent from every patient shown
Access to both the pre-operative wait and the moment of bandage removal

suggestions.name: A rural district hospital or temple hall hosting a visiting eye camp
suggestions.why: Mobile cataract-surgery camps are a long-running form of rural outreach in Sri Lanka and are held periodically in under-served districts.
suggestions.verify: A specific camp, its organisers and dates are unconfirmed and must be found.

risks: Turning patients into 'miracle' spectacle or charity advertising
Filming distress or failed outcomes without full consent
drop_if: No camp falls within the filming window
Patients or the medical team are unwilling to be filmed through the whole process

connections.note: Both closing candidates show a condition, sight or fire, finally withdrawn or completed, echoing the group's hand-off that what arises by conditions can also cease by conditions.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
